name: RRB NTPC (Graduate)
fullName: Railway Recruitment Boards – Non-Technical Popular Categories (Graduate Level)
frequency: Annual (as per RRB calendar; separate Graduate and Undergraduate CENs)
approxCandidates: ≈50–60 lakh applicants per graduate-level cycle (approx.; exact figure for CEN 06/2025 not officially confirmed)
eligibility: Graduate degree from a recognised university; 18–33 yrs (age relaxation as per rules)

notification.summary: Current graduate-level cycle is CEN 06/2025 (5,810 posts such as Goods Train Manager, Station Master, Chief Commercial-cum-Ticket Supervisor, Senior Clerk-cum-Typist). CBT 1 was held 16–27 March 2026, CBT 1 result was declared on 11 June 2026 and CBT 2 was scheduled for 10 July 2026; CBAT/typing skill test and DV are the remaining stages. A fresh graduate-level CEN is expected under the next RRB calendar but had not been notified as of the check date.

pattern.notes: No sectional time limit. Negative marking of 1/3 mark per wrong answer. CBT 1 is qualifying (shortlisting for CBT 2); marks are normalised across shifts. Minimum qualifying percentage: UR/EWS 40%, OBC/SC 30%, ST 25%. PwBD scribe candidates get 120 minutes.

trendAnalysis.summary: Across the 2024–25 (CEN 05/2024) and March 2026 (CEN 06/2025) graduate CBT 1 shifts, overall difficulty has been easy-to-moderate. General Awareness is the deciding section: memory-based analyses rate it the toughest, with 10–16 current-affairs questions per shift (last 6–12 months: schemes, sports, awards, summits) followed by science, history and polity (specific Articles/amendments). Mathematics is calculation-heavy but conceptually basic (percentage, SI/CI, profit-loss, time-work, mensuration, simple trigonometry). Reasoning is the most scoring section with analogies, series, coding-decoding, syllogism and short puzzles. Good attempts for graduate shifts are reported around 78–88 out of 100.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the NTPC CBT 1 papers of the current cycles: CEN 05/2024 Graduate (5–24 Jun 2025), CEN 06/2024 Undergraduate (7 Aug–9 Sep 2025, same syllabus and section mix) and CEN 06/2025 Graduate (16–27 Mar 2026). No NTPC CBT was held in 2024, so the blueprint covers 2025 and 2026. RRB bars sharing of live questions; web searches (Oct 2026) returned only difficulty/good-attempt analyses (Careers360, PracticeMock, AspirantMitraa) without question-level detail, and WebFetch of papers was not possible. Question TYPES were therefore described from the writer's own knowledge of NTPC papers and memory-based topic lists. All patterns are paraphrased.

archetypes.pattern: Recent sports events – winner/host/venue of tournaments and medal events of the last 12 months
New government schemes and missions – target group, benefit or launching ministry
Space, defence and security milestones – ISRO missions, military operations, commemorative days
Awards and honours announced recently – Jnanpith, Bharat Ratna, Padma, film and literary awards
International summits and organisations – host city, new members, India's role
Indian Railways developments – safety systems, new bridges/lines, train services
Ancient/medieval India – inscriptions, dynasties and their notable rulers/expeditions
Modern India – battles, Governors-General and their policies/acts
National movement – leaders, organisations they founded, movements and sessions
Which Article deals with a given right, emergency or institution
Constitutional amendments and features borrowed from other constitutions
Constitutional bodies and offices – appointment, removal, functions (CAG, EC, Governor)
Indian physical geography – states by area, passes, rivers, Tropic of Cancer states
Soils, crops, minerals and multipurpose projects of India
World/physical geography – atmosphere layers, latitudes, oceans, continents
Human body – glands, organs, brain parts, vitamins and diseases
Everyday chemistry – chemical names/formulas, fuels, pH of common substances
Physics basics – SI units, lens/mirror facts, everyday phenomena
Cell biology, plant processes and genetics (Mendel ratios)
Monetary policy and taxation – repo/CRR, RBI role, GST facts, budget terms
Classical/folk dances, festivals and monuments matched with states
Sports trophies, terms and venues matched with games
Computer fundamentals – shortcuts, memory types, input/output devices, units
Headquarters of international organisations, important days, books and authors
Protected areas, biosphere reserves and environmental conventions
Unit digit of a product of large powers using cyclicity
Least number to be added/subtracted for divisibility; remainders
Sums of series of natural/odd/even numbers, factors and primes
Simplify decimal/fraction expressions with BODMAS and "of"
HCF/LCM product rule, greatest/least number with given remainders
Basic percentage – x% of y, percentage equations (a% of A = b% of B), consumption–expenditure
Exam pass/fail with overlap, elections and population change
Division of a sum in simple, fractional or chained ratios
Ages and mixtures in ratio form
Average with a wrongly recorded value, inclusion/exclusion, overlapping groups
Mark-up and discount – profit %, or marked price for a target gain
Same SP with gain/loss, dishonest weights, chain transactions
Simple interest – SI, rate, time or principal
Compound interest – amounts in consecutive years, CI − SI difference
Work done by two persons with efficiency ratio or one leaving midway
Pipes and cisterns with one pipe closed after some time
Trains crossing a pole/platform or each other
Relative speed – chase problems, average speed, boats
2-D figures – square/rectangle/circle/triangle area and perimeter
3-D solids – cylinder/cone/sphere surface area and volume
Algebraic identities with x + 1/x, a + b and ab
Linear equations and value of an algebraic expression
Trigonometric ratios from a given ratio and standard identities
Angles in triangles and circles (angle at centre vs. circumference, cyclic quadrilateral)
Small table of yearly figures – percentage change, average or ratio; mean/median/mode
Word analogy – tool/function, need/fulfilment, worker/place relations
Number analogy – n², n³, n² ± 1 relations
Odd word out from a category (instruments, cities, organs)
Odd number/number pair/letter cluster out (primes, squares, fixed gaps)
Number series with growing differences or ×k (+/−) patterns
Letter and alphanumeric cluster series with fixed shifts
Letter-shift coding – uniform, alternating or position-based (+1, +2, +3 …) shifts
Number coding – alphabet positions concatenated/summed, letter-to-digit codes
Symbol substitution followed by BODMAS evaluation
Interchange two signs/numbers to make an equation correct
Pointing/introduction statements
Family chain of 4–5 people – how is X related to Y
Walk path with turns – distance and direction from start
Shadow at sunrise/sunset or facing direction after turns
Two statements and two conclusions (All/Some/No)
Three statements with two conclusions, including negative chains
Linear row of 5–8 people with position/neighbour clues
Comparison/ordering puzzles (heights, marks) and circular seating
Two-set counting with both/neither
Select the diagram that represents three classes
Statement with two conclusions – which follow
Advertisement/notice with two assumptions – which are implicit
Letter position in the (reversed) alphabet, letters between positions
Arrange words in dictionary order – first/last/middle word
Missing number in a 3 × 3 grid or figure where rows follow a² + b², a × b + c type rules
Mirror or water image of a letter–number combination or clock
Day of the week for a date using odd days
Angle between the hands of a clock at a given time

resources.notes: RRBs do not keep a permanent PYQ archive. After each CBT the question papers, provisional answer keys and candidate response sheets are published for a limited objection window via the regional RRB websites (e.g. https://www.rrbcdg.gov.in, linked from https://www.rrbapply.gov.in). Some cycles also provide a mock-test link on regional RRB sites shortly before the CBT. Shift-wise memory-based papers are available from coaching publishers (unofficial).

questions.question: India observes 'National Space Day' every year on 23 August to commemorate which event?
options: Launch of Aryabhata, India's first satellite
Soft landing of Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander on the Moon
Launch of the Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter) Mission
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander soft-landed near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023; the Government of India declared 23 August as National Space Day.

questions.question: At the G20 Leaders' Summit held in New Delhi in September 2023, which organisation was admitted as a permanent member of the G20?
questions.explanation: Under India's presidency, the African Union was made a permanent member of the G20 at the New Delhi Summit (9–10 September 2023).

questions.question: Which Indian shooter won two bronze medals at the Paris 2024 Olympics, becoming the first Indian after Independence to win two medals at a single Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: Manu Bhaker won bronze in the women's 10 m air pistol and in the 10 m air pistol mixed team event (with Sarabjot Singh) at Paris 2024.

questions.question: Who proclaimed the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind) at Singapore in October 1943?
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose proclaimed the Provisional Government of Azad Hind on 21 October 1943 in Singapore.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT part of the combined forces that fought against the East India Company in the Battle of Buxar (1764)?
questions.explanation: At Buxar the Company defeated Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula (Nawab of Awadh) and Mughal emperor Shah Alam II. Siraj-ud-Daulah had been killed after the Battle of Plassey in 1757.

questions.question: The Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription), composed by the court poet Harisena, describes the achievements of which ruler?
questions.explanation: Harisena, court poet of Samudragupta, composed the Prayag Prashasti engraved on the Allahabad pillar describing Samudragupta's conquests.

questions.question: Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976), on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation, inserted Part IV-A (Article 51A) with Fundamental Duties.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution can the President proclaim a Financial Emergency?
questions.explanation: Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency; Article 352 is National Emergency and Article 356 is President's Rule in a State.

questions.question: The idea of a 'Concurrent List' in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the constitution of which country?
questions.explanation: The Concurrent List (and joint sitting of Parliament) was borrowed from Australia; Directive Principles came from Ireland and the federation with a strong Centre from Canada.

questions.question: Which is the largest state of India by area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan (about 3.42 lakh km²) is the largest state by area, followed by Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

questions.question: The Nathu La pass, an important trade route between India and China (Tibet), is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Nathu La lies on the Sikkim–Tibet border and is used for border trade and the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following Indian states?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. It does not pass through Odisha.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of baking soda?
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO₃. Na₂CO₃ is washing soda (in its decahydrate form).

questions.question: Which part of the human brain is mainly responsible for maintaining posture and balance of the body?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum (part of the hindbrain) coordinates voluntary movements and maintains posture and equilibrium.

questions.question: A lens has a power of −2.5 D. Which of the following correctly describes it?
options: Concave lens of focal length 40 cm
Convex lens of focal length 40 cm
Concave lens of focal length 25 cm
Convex lens of focal length 25 cm
questions.explanation: f = 1/P = 1/(−2.5) m = −0.4 m = −40 cm. A negative focal length means a concave (diverging) lens.

questions.question: In Mendel's dihybrid cross between pure-breeding round-yellow and wrinkled-green pea plants, the phenotypic ratio obtained in the F₂ generation is:
questions.explanation: Selfing the F₁ (RrYy) gives 9 round-yellow : 3 round-green : 3 wrinkled-yellow : 1 wrinkled-green.

questions.question: In India, the policy repo rate is decided by:
options: The Monetary Policy Committee of the RBI
questions.explanation: Since 2016 the six-member Monetary Policy Committee constituted under the RBI Act fixes the policy repo rate.

questions.question: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was implemented across India with effect from:
questions.explanation: GST, introduced through the 101st Constitutional Amendment, came into force on 1 July 2017.

questions.question: Kathakali is a classical dance form of which state?
questions.explanation: Kathakali is from Kerala; Bharatanatyam is from Tamil Nadu, Odissi from Odisha and Manipuri from Manipur.

questions.question: The Durand Cup, one of the oldest tournaments in Asia, is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: The Durand Cup, first held in 1888, is a football tournament.

questions.question: In most Windows applications, which keyboard shortcut is used to undo the last action?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + Z undoes; Ctrl + Y redoes, Ctrl + X cuts and Ctrl + U underlines.

questions.question: The International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, has its seat at:
questions.explanation: The ICJ sits in the Peace Palace at The Hague, Netherlands.

questions.question: World Environment Day is observed every year on:
questions.explanation: World Environment Day is on 5 June; 22 April is Earth Day and 16 September is World Ozone Day.

questions.question: Which of the following biosphere reserves is located in Tamil Nadu?
questions.explanation: Gulf of Mannar is in Tamil Nadu; Simlipal is in Odisha, Nokrek in Meghalaya and Pachmarhi in Madhya Pradesh.

questions.question: What is the unit digit of 7³⁵?
questions.explanation: Unit digits of powers of 7 repeat in the cycle 7, 9, 3, 1. 35 = 4×8 + 3, so the unit digit is the 3rd in the cycle, i.e. 3.

questions.question: What is the least number that must be added to 2497 so that the sum is exactly divisible by 13?
questions.explanation: 13 × 192 = 2496, so 2497 leaves remainder 1. Add 13 − 1 = 12 to get 2509 = 13 × 193.

questions.question: Simplify: 48 ÷ 6 × 4 − 3² + 5
The LCM of two numbers is 360 and their HCF is 12. If one of the numbers is 72, the other number is:
questions.explanation: Product of numbers = HCF × LCM = 12 × 360 = 4320. Other number = 4320 ÷ 72 = 60.

questions.question: What is the value of 35% of 240 + 15% of 160?
The price of sugar rises by 25%. By what percentage must a family reduce its consumption so that its expenditure on sugar remains unchanged?
questions.explanation: Required reduction = 25/(100 + 25) × 100 = 20%.

questions.question: ₹7,800 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4. What is B's share?
questions.explanation: 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4 = 6 : 4 : 3 (multiplying by 12). Total 13 parts; one part = 7800/13 = 600. B gets 4 × 600 = ₹2,400.

questions.question: The average of 11 numbers is 36. The average of the first 6 numbers is 32 and that of the last 6 numbers is 40. What is the 6th number?
A shopkeeper marks an article 25% above its cost price and then allows a discount of 12%. What is his profit percentage?
A trader sells two articles for ₹990 each. On one he gains 10% and on the other he loses 10%. What is his overall result?
questions.explanation: CP of first = 990/1.1 = 900; CP of second = 990/0.9 = 1100. Total CP = 2000, total SP = 1980, so loss = ₹20 (1%).

questions.question: What is the simple interest on ₹6,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years?
What is the difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and the simple interest on ₹12,000 at 10% per annum for 3 years?
A can complete a work in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work together for 4 days, after which A leaves. In how many more days will B finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation: Work done in 4 days = 4 × (1/12 + 1/18) = 4 × 5/36 = 5/9. Remaining = 4/9; B needs (4/9) × 18 = 8 days.

questions.question: A train 240 m long is running at 72 km/h. How long will it take to cross a signal pole?
Two trains of lengths 150 m and 210 m are running in opposite directions on parallel tracks at 60 km/h and 48 km/h. In how much time will they completely cross each other?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 60 + 48 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s. Distance = 150 + 210 = 360 m. Time = 360/30 = 12 s.

questions.question: What is the curved surface area of a right circular cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
If x + 1/x = 5, then what is the value of x³ + 1/x³?
If sin θ = 3/5, where θ is an acute angle, then what is the value of tan θ + sec θ?
questions.explanation: cos θ = 4/5, so tan θ = 3/4 and sec θ = 5/4. Sum = 8/4 = 2.

questions.question: Pen : Write :: Knife : ?
questions.explanation: A pen is used to write; similarly a knife is used to cut (tool : function).

questions.question: Select the number that completes the analogy. 7 : 50 :: 9 : ?
questions.explanation: 7² + 1 = 50; similarly 9² + 1 = 82.

questions.question: Select the odd number out: 23, 29, 37, 51
questions.explanation: 23, 29 and 37 are prime numbers; 51 = 3 × 17 is composite.

questions.question: Find the next term: 3, 8, 15, 24, 35, ?
questions.explanation: Terms are n² − 1 for n = 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 → next is 7² − 1 = 48. (Differences 5, 7, 9, 11, 13.)

questions.question: Find the next term: 1, 2, 6, 21, 88, ?
If CAT is coded as DBU, how will DOG be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted one place forward: D→E, O→P, G→H.

questions.question: In a certain code, MANGO is written as OCPIQ. How will APPLE be written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is moved two places forward: A→C, P→R, P→R, L→N, E→G.

questions.question: If '+' means '×', '×' means '−', '−' means '÷' and '÷' means '+', what is the value of 16 − 4 + 3 ÷ 8 × 5?
Pointing to a man, Riya (a girl) said, 'He is the only son of the only son of my grandfather.' How is the man related to Riya?
questions.explanation: The only son of Riya's grandfather is her father. The only son of her father is her brother.

questions.question: Aman walks 8 m north, turns right and walks 5 m, turns right again and walks 14 m, then turns right and walks 5 m. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: Taking the start as (0, 0): north 8 → (0, 8); east 5 → (5, 8); south 14 → (5, −6); west 5 → (0, −6). He is 6 m south of the start.

questions.question:
Statements: All roses are flowers. Some flowers are red.
Conclusions: I. Some roses are red. II. Some flowers are roses.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: 'All roses are flowers' converts to 'Some flowers are roses', so II follows. The red flowers need not include any rose, so I does not follow.

questions.question:
Statements: No pen is a book. All books are copies.
Conclusions: I. Some copies are not pens. II. No copy is a pen.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: The copies that are books cannot be pens, so 'Some copies are not pens' is definite. Copies outside the book region may or may not be pens, so II is not certain.

questions.question: P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing north. R sits in the middle. P sits at the extreme left. T sits to the immediate right of R. Q is not an immediate neighbour of P. Who sits second from the left end?
questions.explanation: Positions 1–5 from left: P = 1, R = 3, T = 4. Q and S take 2 and 5; Q cannot be next to P, so Q = 5 and S = 2.

questions.question: J, K, L, M, N and O sit in a row facing north. K sits third from the left end. Exactly two people sit between K and N. J sits to the immediate left of O. L does not sit at either end. M sits at one of the ends. Who sits exactly between L and J?
questions.explanation: K = 3, so N = 6 (two people between them). M must be at an end, and position 6 is taken, so M = 1. J–O must be adjacent among 2, 4, 5 → J = 4, O = 5. L = 2. Order: M L K J O N, so K sits between L and J.

questions.question: In a group of 60 people, 35 like tea, 30 like coffee and 10 like both. How many people like neither tea nor coffee?
questions.explanation: People liking at least one = 35 + 30 − 10 = 55. Neither = 60 − 55 = 5.

questions.question:
Statement: The railway has introduced online ticket booking to reduce queues at ticket counters.
Conclusions: I. Online booking may reduce crowding at ticket counters. II. All passengers will now book their tickets only online.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: The stated purpose directly supports I. Nothing says counters are closed or that every passenger will switch, so II does not follow.

questions.question: If the English alphabet is written in reverse order, which letter will be 7th from the left?
questions.explanation: Reverse order: Z, Y, X, W, V, U, T … The 7th letter is T (equivalently 27 − 7 = 20th letter of the normal order).

questions.question: 15 August 2026 falls on a Saturday. On which day of the week did 15 August 2025 fall?
questions.explanation: From 15 Aug 2025 to 15 Aug 2026 there are 365 days (February 2026 has 28 days), i.e. 52 weeks + 1 day. So 15 Aug 2025 was one day before Saturday: Friday.

questions.question: In September 2024 India won gold medals in both the Open and the Women's sections of the 45th Chess Olympiad. Where was it held?
questions.explanation: The 45th Chess Olympiad was held in Budapest, Hungary; India won both team golds for the first time. (Chennai hosted the 44th Olympiad in 2022.)

questions.question: The 'Ayushman Vay Vandana Card', launched in October 2024 under AB PM-JAY, provides health cover of up to ₹5 lakh to:
options: All senior citizens aged 70 years and above, irrespective of income
Only BPL senior citizens above 60 years
questions.explanation: The October 2024 expansion of Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY covers every citizen aged 70+ regardless of income, with up to ₹5 lakh per family per year.

questions.question: India's 'Operation Sindoor' in May 2025 was launched in response to the terrorist attack at which place?
questions.explanation: On 7 May 2025 India struck terror infrastructure in Pakistan and PoK under Operation Sindoor, after the 22 April 2025 terror attack on tourists at Pahalgam (J&K).

questions.question: Who was named for the 59th Jnanpith Award, announced in March 2025?
questions.explanation: Hindi writer Vinod Kumar Shukla of Chhattisgarh received the 59th Jnanpith. Gulzar and Rambhadracharya shared the 58th; Damodar Mauzo received the 57th.

questions.question: The 17th BRICS Summit was held in July 2025 in which city?
questions.explanation: Brazil hosted the 17th BRICS Summit at Rio de Janeiro on 6–7 July 2025. Kazan (Russia) hosted the 16th in 2024 and Johannesburg the 15th in 2023.

questions.question: 'Kavach', being deployed across Indian Railways, is:
options: A mobile app for unreserved ticket booking
An indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection system
questions.explanation: Kavach, developed by RDSO with Indian industry, automatically applies brakes if a loco pilot fails to act, to prevent collisions and signal passing at danger.

questions.question: Which Chola ruler sent a naval expedition to the Srivijaya kingdom in South-East Asia?
questions.explanation: Rajendra Chola I (1014–1044 CE) led the naval expedition against Srivijaya around 1025 CE and also took the title "Gangaikonda".

questions.question: Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur were annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse during the tenure of which Governor-General?
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie (1848–56) applied the Doctrine of Lapse to annex states whose rulers died without a natural heir. Wellesley is linked with the Subsidiary Alliance.

questions.question: Who founded the 'Servants of India Society' in 1905?
questions.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in Pune in 1905 to train workers for national service.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India abolishes titles (except military and academic distinctions)?
questions.explanation: Article 18 abolishes titles. Article 17 abolishes untouchability, Article 14 guarantees equality before law and Article 21 protects life and personal liberty.

questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the constitution of:
questions.explanation: The idea of DPSP (Part IV) came from the Irish Constitution. Fundamental Rights were inspired by the USA and parliamentary government by the UK.

questions.question: Who appoints the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: Under Article 148, the CAG is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.

questions.question: Which soil of India is also known as 'regur' soil?
questions.explanation: Black soil, formed from Deccan basalt, is called regur; it retains moisture and is ideal for cotton.

questions.question: The ozone layer is found mainly in which layer of the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Most atmospheric ozone lies in the stratosphere at about 15–35 km altitude, where it absorbs harmful UV radiation.

questions.question: Which gland is called the 'master gland' of the human body?
questions.explanation: The pituitary secretes hormones that regulate several other endocrine glands, hence "master gland".

questions.question: LPG used as cooking gas mainly consists of:
questions.explanation: LPG is mainly butane (with some propane) liquefied under pressure. CNG is mainly methane.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
questions.explanation: Charge is measured in coulomb (1 C = 1 A × 1 s). Ampere is the unit of current, volt of potential difference and ohm of resistance.

questions.question: In a plant cell, photosynthesis takes place in the:
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which traps light energy to make glucose from CO₂ and water. Mitochondria carry out respiration.

questions.question: When the Reserve Bank of India cuts the repo rate, it generally aims to:
options: Absorb excess liquidity from the banking system
Increase the cash reserve ratio of banks
Raise interest rates on bank loans
Make loans cheaper and encourage spending
questions.explanation: A lower repo rate reduces the cost at which banks borrow from the RBI, so lending rates tend to fall and credit and spending rise.

questions.question: Sattriya, one of the recognised classical dance forms of India, belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Sattriya was introduced by Srimanta Sankaradeva in the sattras (monasteries) of Assam and was recognised as a classical dance in 2000.

questions.question: The Ranji Trophy is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: The Ranji Trophy is India's premier domestic first-class cricket championship, named after K. S. Ranjitsinhji.

questions.question: Which of the following is a volatile memory of a computer?
questions.explanation: RAM loses its contents when power is switched off. ROM, hard disks and flash (pen) drives retain data.

questions.question: The headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO) is located in:
questions.explanation: WHO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. UN HQ is in New York, UNESCO in Paris and IAEA in Vienna.

questions.question: The Ramsar Convention is concerned with the conservation of:
questions.explanation: The Ramsar Convention (1971, Ramsar, Iran) is for the conservation and wise use of wetlands. Ozone is covered by the Vienna Convention/Montreal Protocol.

questions.question: What is the unit digit of (2467)¹⁵³ × (341)⁷²?
questions.explanation: Unit digit of 7ⁿ repeats every 4 (7, 9, 3, 1). 153 = 4 × 38 + 1, so 7¹⁵³ ends in 7. Any power of a number ending in 1 ends in 1. 7 × 1 = 7.

questions.question: What is the least number that must be subtracted from 8961 so that the result is exactly divisible by 23?
questions.explanation: 8961 = 23 × 389 + 14, so subtracting 14 gives 8947 = 23 × 389. (Adding 9 would also make it divisible, which is the trap.)

questions.question: What is the sum of all odd numbers from 1 to 59?
questions.explanation: There are 30 odd numbers from 1 to 59, and the sum of the first n odd numbers is n² = 30² = 900.

questions.question: What is the greatest number that divides 154, 282 and 346, leaving a remainder of 2 in each case?
If 20% of A is equal to 30% of B, then A : B is:
In an examination, 35% of the candidates failed in Mathematics, 25% failed in English and 10% failed in both. What percentage of the candidates passed in both subjects?
questions.explanation: Failed in at least one subject = 35 + 25 − 10 = 50%. Passed in both = 100 − 50 = 50%.

questions.question: ₹7,000 is divided among A, B and C such that A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5. What is C's share?
The average marks of 40 students were found to be 62. Later it was discovered that one student's marks had been entered as 84 instead of 48. What is the correct average?
questions.explanation: Total was overstated by 84 − 48 = 36. Correct average = 62 − 36/40 = 62 − 0.9 = 61.1.

questions.question: A shopkeeper allows a 20% discount on the marked price and still gains 12%. If the cost price of an article is ₹500, what is its marked price?
A dishonest dealer claims to sell his goods at a 10% loss on cost price, but uses a weight of 750 g in place of 1 kg. What is his actual gain or loss per cent?
questions.explanation: He gives goods costing ₹75 (for every ₹100 of 1 kg) and charges ₹90. Gain = 15/75 × 100 = 20%.

questions.question: A sum of money at compound interest (compounded annually) amounts to ₹6,050 in 2 years and to ₹6,655 in 3 years. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.explanation: Interest in the 3rd year = 6655 − 6050 = 605, which is interest on 6050 for one year. Rate = 605/6050 × 100 = 10%.

questions.question: A is twice as efficient as B. Working together, they finish a piece of work in 14 days. In how many days can A alone finish it?
questions.explanation: Let B do 1 unit/day and A 2 units/day. Total work = 3 × 14 = 42 units. A alone = 42/2 = 21 days.

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 6 hours and pipe B in 8 hours. Both are opened together, but B is closed after 2 hours. How much more time will A take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: In 2 hours both fill 2 × (1/6 + 1/8) = 2 × 7/24 = 7/12. Remaining 5/12 is filled by A in (5/12) ÷ (1/6) = 2.5 hours.

questions.question: A thief runs at 8 km/h. A policeman starts chasing him 10 minutes later at 10 km/h. In how many minutes after starting will the policeman catch the thief?
questions.explanation: Head start = 8 × 10/60 = 4/3 km. Relative speed = 2 km/h. Time = (4/3)/2 = 2/3 h = 40 minutes.

questions.question: The diagonal of a square is 12√2 cm. What is the area of the square?
questions.explanation: Diagonal = a√2 → a = 12 cm. Area = 12² = 144 cm². (Equivalently, area = d²/2 = 288/2.)

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, chord AB subtends an angle of 110° at the centre. What angle does AB subtend at a point C on the major arc?
questions.explanation: The angle at the circumference on the major arc is half the angle at the centre: 110°/2 = 55°. (A point on the minor arc would give 180° − 55° = 125°.)

questions.question: The production of a factory (in thousand units) was 45 in 2021, 52 in 2022, 50 in 2023, 60 in 2024 and 65 in 2025. What is the percentage increase in production from 2023 to 2025?
questions.explanation: Increase = 65 − 50 = 15 thousand units on a base of 50. Percentage = 15/50 × 100 = 30%. (Dividing by 65 gives 23.1%.)

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word.
Hunger : Food :: Thirst : ?
questions.explanation: Hunger is satisfied by food; thirst is satisfied by water.

questions.question:
Select the number that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number.
17 : 289 :: 23 : ?
questions.explanation: 17² = 289. Similarly 23² = 529.

questions.question: Select the odd one out.
questions.explanation: Tabla, mridangam and dholak are percussion (drum) instruments; the sitar is a string instrument.

questions.question:
Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series?
4, 6, 12, 30, 90, ?
questions.explanation: The multipliers are ×1.5, ×2, ×2.5, ×3, so next is ×3.5: 90 × 3.5 = 315.

questions.question:
Select the term that will come next in the following series.
B2D, E5G, H8J, ?
questions.explanation: Each part increases by 3: B→E→H→K, 2→5→8→11, D→G→J→M. Next = K11M.

questions.question: In a certain code language, WATER is written as XCWIW. How will FLOWER be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The 1st, 2nd, 3rd … letters are moved +1, +2, +3, +4, +5: W→X, A→C, T→W, E→I, R→W. FLOWER: F+1 = G, L+2 = N, O+3 = R, W+4 = A, E+5 = J, R+6 = X → GNRAJX.

questions.question: In a certain code language, FAN is written as 6114 and BAT is written as 2120. How will CUP be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its alphabet position written in order: F = 6, A = 1, N = 14 → 6114. CUP = 3, 21, 16 → 32116.

questions.question:
Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?
9 + 8 × 4 − 6 ÷ 2 = 29
questions.explanation: Interchanging 8 and 6: 9 + 6 × 4 − 8 ÷ 2 = 9 + 24 − 4 = 29 ✓. The other swaps give 73, 23.5 and 33.5.

questions.question: A is the son of B. C is the daughter of A. D is the wife of A. E is the mother of D. How is E related to C?
questions.explanation: D is A's wife and hence C's mother. E is D's mother, so E is C's mother's mother – maternal grandmother.

questions.question: One morning after sunrise, Suresh was standing facing a pole. The shadow of the pole fell exactly to his right. Which direction was Suresh facing?
questions.explanation: In the morning the sun is in the east, so shadows fall towards the west. If west is on his right, Suresh is facing south.

questions.question:
Statements:
Some doors are windows.
All windows are walls.
No wall is a roof.
Conclusions:
I. Some doors are walls.
II. No window is a roof.
Which of the conclusions logically follow(s)?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: The doors that are windows are walls, so I follows. All windows are walls and no wall is a roof, so no window is a roof – II also follows.

questions.question: Six friends U, V, W, X, Y and Z sit in a row facing north. W sits third from the right end. Only one person sits between W and Z. U sits at the extreme left end. Y sits to the immediate right of U. V sits to the immediate left of W. Who sits between W and Z?
questions.explanation: Positions from the left: U = 1, Y = 2, W = 4 (third from right). Z is two places from W: position 2 is taken, so Z = 6. V = 3 (immediate left of W), leaving X = 5, which is between W and Z.

questions.question: Among five boys P, Q, R, S and T, Q is taller than R but shorter than T. P is taller than T. S is the shortest of all. Who is the second tallest?
questions.explanation: From the clues: P > T > Q > R, and S is the shortest. Order: P, T, Q, R, S. The second tallest is T.

questions.question: Which of the following best represents the relationship among: Indians, Doctors, Singers?
options: Three circles, each intersecting the other two
One circle inside another, with the third separate
questions.explanation: Some Indians are doctors, some Indians are singers and some doctors are singers; a person can belong to all three. So three mutually intersecting circles.

questions.question:
Statement: 'Book your train tickets online and avoid long queues at the counter.' – an advertisement of a railway ticketing portal.
Assumptions:
I. Many passengers would like to avoid standing in long queues.
II. Passengers can access the online booking facility.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit?
options: Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
questions.explanation: The advertisement assumes people dislike long queues (I) and that they are able to book online (II); otherwise the appeal would be pointless. Both are implicit.

questions.question: Which of the following words will come LAST when arranged in English dictionary order?
questions.explanation: Order: Mischief (misc-), Miserable (mise-), Missile (missi-l), Mission (missi-o). Mission comes last.

questions.question:
Find the missing number. In each row the third number is obtained from the first two by the same rule.
Row 1: 5, 7, 74
Row 2: 3, 9, 90
Row 3: 6, 4, ?
questions.explanation: Third number = (first)² + (second)²: 25 + 49 = 74, 9 + 81 = 90, so 36 + 16 = 52.
